sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the verse "in Your light we see light" refers to Torah and Israel, where Torah is the "length" and the revealed light is the root of Israel, which is higher than Torah but revealed through it.

translations.translation: And the verse continues, "we see light,"
which is above even length,
to the point that length is only a preparation for the light that is seen through it
(as above from the maamar).
And the explanation of this can be understood based on the known principle29
regarding Torah and the souls of Israel,
that the root of Israel is above the root of Torah30,
as it is stated in Tanna D'vei Eliyahu31
Two things preceded the world: Torah and Israel,
and I do not know which of them came first,
but when He says "Command the children of Israel," "Speak to the children of Israel,"
I say that Israel preceded.
However, the souls of Israel were drawn down and descended into a state of independent existence,
like a son
("You are children to Hashem your G-d"32)
who, despite being from the essence of the father,
is a separate entity33,
while Torah, even as it is drawn down below, is unified with Him, blessed be He,
"The Torah and the Holy One, blessed be He, are entirely one"34.
And this is the reason that the virtue of Israel
(who preceded Torah)
is revealed through the Torah
(for in the Torah it is said, "Command the children of Israel,"
"Speak to the children of Israel"),
for the souls,
as they are in themselves,
being a separate entity,
their root is in concealment,
but not so Torah,
which is one with the Holy One, blessed be He,
it is a level of revelation
("and Torah is light"),
and through the Torah is revealed
(also)
the root of Israel.
And based on this, it can be said that the two matters of "in Your light we see light" are Torah and Israel.
"Your light" is Torah
(as above),
and the light that is seen through "Your light" is the root of Israel that is revealed through the Torah35.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that "Arise, shine, for your light has come" refers to two lights—the light of Israel themselves and the light they shine—paralleling the soul and body, where the soul's love is natural and the body's chosenness is from the Essence.

translations.translation: And this is "Arise, shine, for your light has come,"
for these two matters
("your light" and "your light" [in the sense of length])
are analogous to the two matters of "in Your light we see light"
(as above at the beginning of the maamar).
"Your light" [orech],
the light of Israel themselves,
is like "in Your light"
(Your light),
and "Arise, shine" [uri],
the light that Israel shine,
is like the light that is seen through "Your light"
(which is above "Your light").
And this will be understood based on what is explained elsewhere36
regarding soul and body,
that regarding souls it is written32
"You are children to Hashem your G-d"37,
and therefore,
the love and attachment of the Holy One, blessed be He, to Israel by virtue of their soul is like a natural love, so to speak
(like the love of a father for his son).
That is,
the root of this love is from a level where the place of the beloved is relevant,
and it is not from His very Essence.
However, the love and attachment of the Holy One, blessed be He, to Israel by virtue of their body,
is
(not due to the virtue of the body,
nor even the virtue of "son,"
an essential virtue,
but rather)
due to the fact that the Holy One, blessed be He, chose the body of Israel38,
with His free choice,
for this choice is from His very Essence.
However,
the virtue of the soul
(which is a child to the Holy One, blessed be He)
is revealed,
but not so the virtue of the body
(in which is the choice of the Essence)
is concealed.
And through the soul working with the body,
its virtue is revealed in it,
the choice of the Essence.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that "Arise, shine, for your light has come" means that through the light of the soul, one must work with the body to reveal a higher light than that of the soul itself.

translations.translation: And based on this, we can explain "Arise, shine, for your light has come,"
that "your light" is the light of the soul,
and "Arise, shine" is that through the light of the soul
("for your light has come")
she must work with the body and illuminate it,
so that through this a matter more elevated than the light of the soul is revealed
("your light"),
as explained above
(section 2)
regarding "in Your light we see light,"
that the light seen through "Your light" is more elevated than "Your light."
